novelty_flags.label: prop:causal-distance-identification
novelty_flags.one_line: Its displayed identification functional is exactly the anchor paper's Theorem 1; fixing one outcome surface is not a separately substantive theorem-level advance.

novelty_flags.label: thm:rectifiable-exact-frontier and proposal headline
novelty_flags.one_line: The claim to close the anchor's printed conjecture is only on the stronger uniform-local-mass subclass, so it is not yet a same-class tightening of Theorem 6; either prove the rate under the anchor class or frame this as a primitive-subclass result.

novelty_flags.label: thm:smooth-exact-frontier gap comparison
novelty_flags.one_line: The cited Theorem 3(ii) gives its uniform bias bound only on the interior B_o and under an explicit two-intersection condition, not merely from the proposal's stated global smooth embedding and reach assumptions over all of B.

soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-local-mass
soundness_flags.one_line: Its upper bound is implied by ass:density-envelope: P(X in A_t,P intersect B_2(x,r)) is at most pi L r^2, so retain only the lower local-mass requirement or remove c_+ from the class.

soundness_flags.label: thm:rectifiable-exact-frontier and thm:smooth-exact-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: Both attainment claims use a degree-p, kernel-K estimator, but their constants are claimed to depend only on class constants while p and K are neither fixed in the statements nor included in the constant dependence.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 256 (2026), article 106266, author-hosted journal PDF
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5, Theorem 1; p. 7, Theorem 3(ii); pp. 10-11, Theorem 6 and the paragraph immediately following its attaining-estimator display
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 1 states the displayed distance-identification limit. Theorem 3(ii) requires an interior B_o and a uniform two-intersection premise for its uniform h^m bias conclusion. Theorem 6 gives an n^{-1/4} lower bound, and the paper says its log^{1/4} gap is conjectured unimprovable because its lower bound is pointwise.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the two-sided local-mass assumption by its genuinely additional lower-mass half, and explicitly derive the upper half from the density envelope.

Either establish a transfer from the anchor's Gram condition to a primitive local-mass condition, or change the headline and comparator language to say the logarithmic frontier is resolved on a transparent stronger subclass rather than that the printed conjecture is closed outright.

Make the smooth theorem's upper route match its class: restrict the estimand to an interior curve B_o or add and use a uniform two-intersection/end-point condition, then give the smooth packing construction under that exact class.

Delete the standalone identification proposition as a claimed contribution and state its one-regression embedding as a submodel lemma inside each minimax theorem; fix p and K and expose their constant dependence.

recommended_next_step: Revise the comparator scope, smooth-class upper assumptions, redundant mass condition, and estimator-constant quantification before advancing to Stage 0.
